item.title: A bifunctional silazane additive for simultaneous HF scavenging and dual-interface stabilization in high-voltage lithium metal batteries
item.description:

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using TMDS, a bifunctional silazane additive, to simultaneously scavenge HF and stabilize both electrode interfaces via a Si-containing, LiF-rich CEI and robust LiF SEI. Its significance: suppressing LiPF6 hydrolysis enables >1500 h Li‖Li cycling, and 1 wt% TMDS optimizes high-voltage Li‖NCM811 cycling and rate performance.
🏷 silazane additive · HF scavenging · lithium metal battery · CEI/SEI stabilization · LiF-rich interphase

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | ⭐ Review
💡 The novelty lies in systematically deriving electrolyte design principles specifically for aqueous zinc batteries to overcome poor Zn reversibility. Its significance is providing a rational framework guiding electrolyte selection and engineering, enabling safer, low-cost, sustainable large-scale energy storage and accelerating practical adoption of this promising technology.
🏷 aqueous zinc battery · electrolyte design · Zn reversibility · large-scale storage · design principles

item.title: Experimental Insights into the Limiting Mechanism of Vacancy Transport in Sodium Metal Anodes for Solid State Batteries

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in experimentally identifying the limiting mechanism of vacancy transport in Na metal anodes, moving beyond theoretical predictions. This is significant because contact loss during stripping limits solid-state battery performance; clarifying vacancy transport provides mechanistic insight essential for designing stable Na-metal/ceramic interfaces and advancing safe, long-life solid-state batteries.
🏷 sodium metal anode · solid-state battery · vacancy transport · contact loss · ceramic electrolyte

💡 The novelty lies in embedding LaCl3 nanocrystals within an amorphous Li–Al–O–Cl matrix, creating a composite electrolyte that combines high ionic conductivity (>1 mS cm–1) with exceptional thermal stability (solid at 150 °C, where baseline LAOC melts). This enables stable ASSB operation at 80 °C, unlike LAOC cells. The strategy of reinforcing a soft amorphous matrix with a rigid crystalline phase offers a cost-effective pathway for thermally robust, high-performance solid-state electrolytes.
